title: Siblings
hookLine: from Cain to Joseph, the Torah is honest about siblings; reconciliation is possible
tomorrow: once, God changed someone's words on purpose. to keep what?

lines: THEY KNOW WHICH BUTTON TO PRESS.
DOES ANY PAIR FIND ITS WAY BACK?
cards: Siblings know exactly which button to press, because they were there when it was installed. The Torah knows it too. Its first brothers, Cain and Abel, end in a field with one of them dead.
Isaac and Ishmael are sent apart. Jacob runs from Esau. Joseph's brothers sell him.
Not a flattering record. So does any pair find its way back?

teach.b: Two do. Jacob, after years away, limps toward Esau expecting the worst. And Genesis says Esau "ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him; and they wept."
Then Joseph, in Egypt, with the brothers who sold him standing in front of him, not knowing who he is.
He sends everyone else out, and says: "I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt." He doesn't erase what they did.

teach.h: HE NAMES IT, AND STILL SAYS BROTHER.
teach.b: He names it, and still calls them brothers. Notice what each reunion took. Esau had to set down a grudge he'd carried for years.

Joseph had to stop hiding: until that moment he'd spoken to his brothers through an interpreter, under an Egyptian name. Something to tell a friend tonight: the reunion begins when Joseph drops the translator.

And a psalm sings what all of it is reaching for: "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!" The Torah doesn't pretend siblings are easy. It just won't say they're over.

how: Jewish tradition encourages repair between family members, especially before Yom Kippur, when people seek forgiveness from those they've hurt; Psalm 133, 'how good and how pleasant', is also sung as a song.

o: close friends who call each other family
cousins raised together in one household
brothers and sisters, fights and reunions both

games.q: the Torah's siblings — tap the pairs.

s: the Torah's brothers mostly get along
from Cain and Abel to Joseph, it tells the fights honestly.
when Joseph reveals himself, he names what his brothers did
'whom ye sold into Egypt', and he still says brother.
Esau stayed angry and refused to see Jacob again
he ran to meet him, embraced him, and they wept.

games.q: two sisters in your friend group haven't spoken since a fight over their late mom's house. one asks if she should reach out first. what fits Genesis 45?
o: reach out, name what happened, and still call her sister.
act like the fight never happened and talk about other things.
wait until the other sister apologizes first.
games.why: Joseph says 'whom ye sold into Egypt' and 'your brother' in one sentence: honest about the wrong, open to the person.

practice: Write by hand the first line of a message to a sibling, or to someone who has been like one. Not the whole repair, only the opening sentence. Joseph's opening was his own name and theirs; yours can be as short as hi, it's me.

wordCard.voice: Siblings: in the Torah, the fights are told honestly, and so are the reunions. Esau's embrace. Joseph's I am your brother.

orig.note: Hebrew: brothers; Psalm 133 sings of brethren dwelling together.

carryVoice: One to keep: brothers can meet again, even after the worst of it. Home and family, eight down.
